positions.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF
positions.thesis: SPY hedge to zero beta

positions.name: GE Vernova
positions.thesis: NRC construction permit for GEV/Hitachi's new reactor design (Sep 29-30) is a concrete regulatory milestone that validates the nuclear growth story, whose coverage share jumped to 49% from 9%. With no earnings next week and only 1.1% gain last week, the news is not fully priced; GLJ's Sell is opinion, not information.

positions.name: Hewlett Packard Enterprise
positions.thesis: HPE's Sep 30 $1.2B Vultr AMD Helios order and raised FY27 networking growth guidance are material positives. Despite a 4.5% intraday pop, the week's return is still negative, suggesting the news is not fully priced. Expect continued outperformance as analysts revise estimates upward.

positions.name: Lumentum
positions.thesis: AI Optics Boom story is gaining share (43% vs 36% 4-wk avg) on laser/OCS demand and margin expansion, supporting a modest long. But no new material event, Bernstein initiation is price-target chatter, and high volatility/sentiment swings limit conviction.

positions.name: Lilly (Eli)
positions.thesis: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 Phase 3 data (Sep 29-30) showed ~50 lb weight loss, with BLA submission Q1 2027; Foundayo and Zepbound beat rivals in EASD comparisons. Multiple FDA approvals and InnoCare deal add momentum. Competitive threats from Novo's CV data and Viking cap upside.

positions.name: Micron Technology
positions.thesis: Micron's Sep 30 Q4 beat with above-Street guidance on AI memory demand confirms the bull case, and the AI memory rally story's coverage share is rising (37% vs 29% avg) with a new AI Memory Boom narrative accelerating. Post-earnings drift should favor MU next week, though Burry's puts and bubble fears cap conviction.

positions.name: Netflix
positions.thesis: Deutsche Bank's Sep 29 upgrade to Buy is a new story now 40% of coverage, and the selloff-debate narrative is fading, suggesting a near-term bounce. But the upgrade came with a lowered target and weak engagement trends persist, capping conviction.

positions.name: Nvidia
positions.thesis: Nvidia's record $150B buyback (Sep 28) and reported China opening for ByteDance/Alibaba GPU purchases are fresh positives, with AI Dominance coverage rising to 50% share. Stock near highs but only +0.75% on week, so news not fully priced; expect relative outperformance.

positions.name: RTX Corporation
positions.thesis: RTX secured a major $20.7B AMRAAM contract on Sep 29 and Pratt & Whitney engine deals, supporting defense growth. With the stock down 6.9% in a month, positive contract news may drive modest outperformance next week, though backlog conversion concerns and fading defense-spending coverage limit upside.

positions.name: Sandisk
positions.thesis: Micron's Sept 30 record FQ4 (revenue +350%, EPS +793%, above high end of guidance) reads across to Sandisk as a NAND peer. SNDK fell 4.8% last week, so the read-across is not yet priced. Sandisk's own AI-storage boom, $14B buyback and $94B contracts reinforce the long.

positions.name: Warner Bros. Discovery
positions.thesis: Paramount and WBD announced the anticipated merger closing date on Sep 30, after settling state antitrust challenges. This materially reduces deal risk and should drive merger-arb interest in WBD next week. Argus downgrade is opinion, not a fundamental offset.

positions.name: Advanced Micro Devices
positions.thesis: AMD's $8.2B World Labs acquisition (Sep 28) triggered a 4% drop and adds integration/dilution risk after a 33% monthly run. HPE's $1.2B Vultr Helios order (Sep 30) is positive, but valuation and fading momentum story likely cap relative upside next week.

positions.name: Broadcom
positions.thesis: AVGO's dominant AI $230B-forecast and Q3-earnings narratives are fading (32% and 16% share vs 42%/37% averages) with post-earnings price-target hikes already priced (stock flat 1w, -3% 1m). A fresh China 'switch review' regulatory risk (Sep 24-28) threatens 17% of sales. Apple deal rise is only a modest offset.

positions.name: Berkshire Hathaway
positions.thesis: Buffett's chairman exit and Howard's appointment add governance uncertainty, while the positive Abel/Alphabet narrative fades. Lennar stake increase is too small to offset. Expect slight underperformance next week.

positions.name: Fair Isaac
positions.thesis: FHFA's Sep 28-29 order letting Fannie/Freddie price mortgages with VantageScore ends FICO's mortgage-scoring monopoly, a structural moat hit. Coverage share jumped to 59% and is still rising; the 20-27% drop prices the headline but not the durable share/price erosion, so relative weakness likely persists next week.

positions.name: Hormel Foods
positions.thesis: Hormel's $1.055B cash Brakebush deal on Sep 30 triggered same-day S&P and Moody's downgrades, raising leverage and funding costs. Fresh negative credit news plus integration risk into cyclical chicken should weigh next week, though the 10% one-month drop prices in some of it.

positions.name: Lululemon Athletica
positions.thesis: Fresh Sep 30 cash-flow skepticism and Sep 25 CEO/bylaw governance changes add to negative sentiment from Sep 3 guidance cut. With no earnings next week, LULU likely underperforms as the market questions cash durability and leadership transition.

positions.name: Oracle Corporation
positions.thesis: Oracle's Sep 24 force majeure on Project Jupiter signals AI data-center delays and cost risk, while the AI debt bubble narrative is rising with Burry's new 2027 puts. The stock has already fallen sharply and Bloom contract was reaffirmed, limiting downside, but news flow remains negative. Expect modest underperformance next week.

positions.name: Constellation Brands
positions.thesis: New earnings story dominates: Q2 on Oct 6 expected EPS decline, negative ESP, and analyst target cuts. Selloff/outlook stories fading, but stock already down 12.8% in a month, so edge is modest. Binary event warrants lower confidence.

positions.name: Walmart
positions.thesis: WMT's news skews negative: Costco's Sep 24 Q4 beat fuels a rising 'Costco over Walmart' comparison (share 18%->30%), two Seeking Alpha downgrades flag peak valuation, Mizuho cut its PT to $125, and pricing scrutiny (Warren patent claim, CEO EDLP letter, DOJ beef probe) adds regulatory overhang. Delivery expansion is the lone positive.
